 Illustration. The forest and land fire situation in Indonesia is not yet completely resolved, but hydrometeorological disasters are starting to loom. (Dibuat dengan AI I Kompas.com/BAL) 
 JAKARTA, KOMPAS.com - The forest and land fire situation in Indonesia is not yet completely resolved, but hydrometeorological disasters are starting to loom.
 The Meteorology, Climatology, and Geophysics Agency (BMKG) predicts the rainy season in Indonesia will begin in November 2026.
 Furthermore, the peak of the rainy season is expected from December 2026 to February 2027.
 "If it starts in November until December, the peak will then occur in December, January, and February," said BMKG Head Teuku Faisal Fathani at the Presidential Complex in Jakarta on Monday (October 26, 2026).
 Even though this year’s rainy season will be shorter than in previous years, the BMKG continues to warn about the potential for hydrometeorological disasters at the end and beginning of the year.
 Hydrometeorological disasters are natural disasters caused by disturbances or changes in weather and climatic conditions in the atmosphere.
 "For the end of this year and the beginning of next year, we must be vigilant regarding wet hydrometeorological disasters," he stated.
 Fires Still Burning
 Amidst the threat of hydrometeorological disasters, fires related to forest and land burning have not yet been extinguished in several regions.
 The BMKG Head mentioned that they are still conducting massive weather modification operations (OMC) to extinguish the fires.
 According to him, the OMC operations related to forest fires constitute one of the largest operations ever conducted in Indonesia.
 "There are nine active aircraft in Central and South Kalimantan, and six aircraft in South Sumatra. We hope that this week will bring wet weather, leading to rain," Teuku emphasized.
 Teuku noted that South Sumatra and Central Kalimantan still have high levels of fire activity compared to other areas.
 "We will work hard to extinguish as many fires as possible," he said.
 According to him, the OMC for extinguishing forest fires combines the use of dry ice with salt (NaCl).
 "Under the direction of the President, this operation is being conducted on a massive scale. We are also using Hercules aircraft, CN-295, and other TNI-owned aircraft," he added.
